key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the chemical components and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps stabilize the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling ink composition and mixing order could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track chemical and surface changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations support rapid oxidation and dissolution by iodine/polyiodides, slower PbI2-driven oxidation, and MAI-mediated surface passivation.
watch_item: The abstract reports a model MAPbI3 precursor study, not device-efficiency or operational-lifetime validation; transfer to other formulations requires testing.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
